changes: Preserved submitted match-4 parent byte-for-byte. One offline proposal only: nominal entry budget 250 -> 125 dollars. Unchanged 21-close warmup, r10>0.006 and r5>0 signal, 1.10 heuristic buffer, ten-decimal rounding, next-close fills, 10bp fee, 5bp slippage and all-or-none cash checks. Candidate manifest rewritten for truthful offline provenance; executable signal unchanged. Predeclared risk/profit criteria passed on reused public development data, so select revised OFFLINE source. No infrastructure, live trading, prior submitted source or current orders changed. This is not a claim of improved alpha.
hypothesis: Changing only the nominal entry budget from 250 to 125 dollars will reduce maximum episode marked drawdown to at most 60% of the parent's, improve mean net episode profit by at least 0.25 dollars on the 33 reused public episodes t=20..52, keep identical entry-signal counts with at least three fills and zero rejections. Otherwise retain the parent. This is a sizing/risk hypothesis, not a new predictive-alpha claim.

result_interpretation: 33 paired dependent episodes: old/new mean net profit -0.662622092910052 / -0.3313110464643449 dollars, improvement 0.3313110464457071 dollars. Maximum marked drawdown 0.01595635695141914 / 0.0079781784760047, approximately half; worst profit -15.956356951419139 / -7.9781784760047 dollars. Both had six signals, six fills, zero rejections. Entry friction totals 2.0035503793262897 / 1.0017751896757883 dollars. Mean benchmark-relative returns -0.0005785506628508972 / -0.00024723961640519046: both still lag the episode benchmark on average. Five stride-seven outcomes: mean profits -0.8850545791014156 / -0.4425272895507078. Negative mean remains; improvement is expected exposure scaling, not timing skill. Neither 33 overlapping windows nor five diagnostic windows establish independent or future effectiveness.
review: Match-4 public scoreboard: equity 992.8983450251793, profit -7.10165497482069, return -0.00710165497482069, one applied trade, zero failures. Benchmark equity 968.7707602879149, profit -31.229239712085132, return -0.031229239712085133. Benchmark gap +0.024127584737264444 (+2.4127584737264444 percentage points). Agent-one won this reported match but lost capital. Weaknesses: momentum can buy failed rallies; prior reused development mean is negative. Quarter-budget exposure partly shields a falling benchmark but neither proves positive alpha nor repairs entry timing. Lower exposure can exacerbate rally underparticipation; this proposal addresses loss magnitude, not forecasting.
shared_tips: For the other agent: distinguish benchmark outperformance from absolute capital preservation; a positive benchmark gap in a falling market can coexist with losses and does not establish a profitable entry signal.

For the other agent: test a single fixed risk-budget ablation with unchanged signal, warmup, fills and cost rates; smaller positions mechanically scale both gains and losses, so reduced drawdown should not be presented as improved forecasting.

For the other agent: declare acceptance thresholds before replay and label reused overlapping windows as dependent development data; known negative returns can make a sizing improvement predictable without providing held-out evidence.

For the other agent: report total fee/slippage dollars as well as identical cost rates and fill counts; a sizing change alters friction dollars even when turnover counts and execution assumptions are unchanged.
